content.user_title: Build Accessible Radix UI Design Systems
content.value_statement: Accessible component libraries are hard to build from headless primitives. This skill guides Radix UI architecture, theming, and component patterns for production React teams.
actual_capabilities: Explains how Radix primitives support accessible dialogs, dropdowns, tabs, selects, tooltips, and accordions.
Shows CSS variables, Tailwind, and CVA strategies for themeable component systems.
Describes compound component patterns, polymorphic asChild usage, and controlled state handling.
Provides accessibility checklists for focus management, ARIA labels, keyboard support, and contrast.
Includes troubleshooting guidance for portals, z-index issues, dialog behavior, and TypeScript errors.
limitations: Focused on React projects because Radix primitives require React hooks.
Does not provide a complete ready-made visual theme or product brand system.
Installation commands remain user-run examples and are not executed by the skill.
Accessibility guidance still requires project-specific testing with real assistive technologies.

use_cases.title: Create a Component Library
use_cases.description: Plan reusable Radix-based components with slots, variants, theming tokens, and accessibility requirements.

use_cases.title: Improve Accessibility Patterns
use_cases.description: Review dialogs, dropdowns, and forms for focus handling, ARIA coverage, keyboard support, and screen reader context.

use_cases.title: Migrate From Styled UI Kits
use_cases.description: Replace opinionated components with headless Radix primitives while preserving design tokens and interaction behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Dialog
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Radix UI dialog component for a React app. Include required parts, accessibility checks, and theme token recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Define Theme Tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Radix UI theming plan using CSS variables and Tailwind. Cover colors, spacing, radius, shadows, and dark mode behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Compound Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Radix compound component API. Check asChild usage, controlled state, accessibility responsibilities, and variant naming.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Full Interaction System
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a production Radix UI interaction system for dialogs, dropdowns, tabs, selects, and tooltips. Include testing, migration, and documentation guidance.

output_examples.input: A team needs a reusable modal pattern for account settings.
output_examples.output: The skill would outline Dialog parts, focus restoration, title and description requirements, overlay behavior, theme tokens, and testing checks.

output_examples.input: A designer wants consistent dropdown menus across a product suite.
output_examples.output: The skill would propose menu structure, item states, keyboard navigation, separators, indicators, collision handling, and variant naming rules.

output_examples.input: A platform team wants to standardize component styling.
output_examples.output: The skill would compare CSS variables, Tailwind classes, and CVA variants, then recommend a maintainable token workflow.

best_practices: Keep Radix accessibility primitives intact and add styling around their expected structure.
Use CSS variables or tokens before adding component-specific visual overrides.
Test keyboard navigation, screen reader labels, focus restoration, and contrast before release.
anti_patterns: Do not skip required Dialog title and description elements.
Do not mix controlled and uncontrolled state in the same Radix root.
Do not override Radix keyboard behavior without replacing equivalent accessibility support.

faq.question: Does this skill generate finished UI components?
faq.answer: It guides component architecture and examples, but final implementation depends on your app, styling system, and requirements.

faq.question: Is it only for React projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance focuses on Radix React primitives, which require React hooks.

faq.question: Can it help with Tailwind-based design systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Tailwind, CSS variables, and CVA patterns for themeable Radix components.

faq.question: Does it replace accessibility testing?
faq.answer: No. It provides checklists and patterns, but teams should still test with keyboards and assistive technologies.

faq.question: Can it support shadcn/ui workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when to use shadcn/ui components and when raw Radix primitives are better.

faq.question: Will it execute install commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. Installation commands are documentation examples that users run only when appropriate.
